f.title: Immediately inform the Minister of unexpected side effects of new drugs
f.statement: Under Regulation 70 of the Food and Drugs Regulations 1975, any person who receives a report of an unexpected side effect, injury, toxicity or sensitivity reaction associated with clinical uses, studies, investigations or tests of a new drug shall immediately inform the Minister and furnish the full information available.

f.title: Apply the serious AE/ADR definition including medically important events
f.statement: A serious AE/ADR is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or is a medically important event or reaction.
f.clause: Pharmacovigilance > Definitions

f.title: Validate ICSRs against the four minimum criteria before reporting
f.statement: Only valid ICSRs qualify for reporting. Suspected ADR reports should be validated before reporting to the NPvC to confirm the minimum criteria: an identifiable patient (initials, ID number, date of birth, age, age group or gender), at least one suspected adverse reaction (an unspecified reaction does not qualify), at least one suspected substance/medicinal product, and at least one identifiable reporter (qualification, name, initials or address). Lacking any of the four elements, the case is incomplete and does not qualify for reporting.
f.clause: Reporting of Suspected Adverse Reactions (Serious and Non-Serious)
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety intake & collection

rows.quote: Only valid Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) qualify for reporting. Suspected ADR reports should be validated before reporting them to the NPvC to make sure that the minimum criteria for reporting are included in the reports.
rows.location: Reporting of Suspected Adverse Reactions (Serious and Non-Serious)

f.title: Record reporter contact details; accept anonymous reporters once confirmed
f.statement: Whenever possible, reporter contact details should be recorded to allow follow-up; if the reporter does not wish to provide contact details, the ICSR should still be considered valid provided the organisation informed of the case could confirm it directly with the reporter.
f.clause: Reporting of Suspected Adverse Reactions (Serious and Non-Serious)

f.title: Follow up incomplete ADR reports to obtain missing information
f.statement: Information in suspected ADR reports that meet the minimum requirements may still be incomplete and must be followed up to obtain additional information significant for scientific evaluation; follow-up should be tailored to collecting the missing information.
f.clause: Reporting of Suspected Adverse Reactions (Serious and Non-Serious)

rows.quote: The information in suspected ADRs may be incomplete when first received, despite having the minimum requirements and therefore must be followed-up to obtain additional detailed information significant for the scientific evaluation of the cases. f.title: Set day zero when any MAH staff first receives the minimum criteria; count calendar days
f.statement: The reporting clock for a valid ICSR starts as soon as information containing the minimum criteria reaches any health care provider or any MAH personnel, including medical representatives; this is day zero, regardless of weekends or public holidays, and reporting timelines are in calendar days.
f.clause: Reporting of Suspected Adverse Reactions (Serious and Non-Serious)

rows.quote: The clock for the reporting of a valid ICSR starts as soon as the information containing the minimum reporting criteria has been brought to the attention of any health care provider or any personnel of the marketing authorization holder, including medical representatives. This date should be considered as day zero. It is the first day when a receiver gains knowledge of a valid ICSR, irrespective of whether the information is received on weekends or public holidays. Please note that reporting timelines are based on calendar days.
